No screenshot of a book page, and no orbit of any NPC. Every browser run here was `critic-w1-library-pages.mjs` at 320x240 with `setRenderRate(0)` — it reads pagination and word counts through the engine's own book path, it does not photograph anything. So I have proven the running engine hands the reading UI real pages instead of `undefined`, and I have NOT looked at how those pages are typeset, wrapped, or contrasted. CLAUDE.md's directive that stills are not enough is unmet for this piece; a critic with a browser should open `the-sap-and-the-ledger` and read it.

I did not reproduce the round-1 critic's RI-DLG03 step-7 count of 46 hits / 45 'question'. Running the item's regex verbatim I get 4 hits (1 on 'question') over `rumours.json` — the scope the item actually names — and 215 hits (131 on 'question') over the whole `game/data/dialogue/**`. Neither is 46, and I do not know their collector's surface (they describe a consumer-traced set of 4,284 rendered strings, which is neither of mine). THE COUNTS DIFFER AND THE FINDING DOES NOT: both derivations agree the regex is unanchored, that most hits are the word 'question', and that the only substantive spoken hit is one RG-VAKH line about a river float, which is clean. Recorded as a disagreement rather than smoothed over; anyone ruling should re-derive.

The evidence-mutation tripwire in `check-authoring-leaks.mjs` fires only on the run where bytes actually change. A check that regenerates its evidence rewrites a CLEAN file to identical bytes, so a second consecutive run of the round-1 shape is silent. That is acceptable — the tripwire fires on exactly the run that destroys evidence, which is the run that matters — but it is a limit, not a total guarantee, and control G2 shows it: the first run exits 4, the leak is already gone, and a second run would exit 0.

A call-site assertion read as TEXT would still be satisfied by a call site inside dead code. `tools/lib/call-site.mjs` says so in its own header and every caller prints the caveat. For the books side this is now moot — the running-browser control C proves consumption entity-side — but for the greetings side the wiring claim is still text-level only.

`check-greeting-voice.mjs` gates 1 of 300 greeting cells and prints that fact on every run. It is a stopgap for a hole no reference item owns (see the corpus proposal), it cannot judge whether writing is GOOD, and it must not be read as having audited the other 299 cells. Its per-group census shows RG-BWC at 95/125 slots carrying a group-exclusive token, the lowest but one of twelve groups — nobody has looked at the other 299 cells and I did not.

repaired_twice_over_deliberately: ROOT CAUSE: `gen-greetings.mjs`'s write is now behind `RUN_DIRECTLY` (`path.resolve(process.argv[1]) === path.resolve(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url))`). An import gets the tables and `buildPools()` and nothing else. Verified: `node --input-type=module -e "await import('.../gen-greetings.mjs')"` leaves the file's md5 unchanged.

INDEPENDENTLY: the check no longer imports ANY generator. It reads `gen-greetings.mjs` as TEXT, strips line comments (essential — both files QUOTE the leaked string in their headers, and a scanner that did not strip comments would flag the explanation of the bug as the bug), brace-matches `const STANCE = {` and `const ADDRESS = {`, and extracts their string literals. Derived this run: STANCE 312 literals, ADDRESS 84.

TRIPWIRE, on top of both: the check SHA-256s every file it is about to read (62 of them), re-hashes after, and exits 4 naming any file whose bytes moved. HAZARDS §31 rule 1 made permanent rather than remembered.

job_4_the_replacement_line_did_not_earn_.the_precision_the_guard_forced_and_i_am_: `check-greeting-voice.mjs` derives token exclusivity from the file and finds `leyawiin` exclusive to RG-BWC but NOT `company` — because RG-NAGA's 'We have eaten better company.' uses the common noun 5 times. job_4_the_replacement_line_did_not_earn_.transplant_test: Hand judgement, stated as such: 'Company time, and Leyawiin bought it.' cannot be said by RG-LEDGER (a Black Marsh writ-house, not a Leyawiin outfit), RG-COURT or RG-EMPIRE.
